It is requested that time necessary for sufficient study of the spawning run and its success be granted prior to a decision on licensing. It is also requested that the applicant perform remedial erosion control of boring locations to prevent further siltation from damaging the spawning success. A survey of Tributaries to Lake Jocassee indicates that Howard Greek is the only stream in South Carolina which has a run. The value of this significant new resource must be assessed by the applicant.
The FPC Staff Discussion (p9 - 2) addresses the need for a fishery mitigation plan for 2.3 miles of treut habitat, i.e. Red Greek. It is our opinion that the overall impact of this project involve a significantly larger amount of habitat less. In addition to the 2.3 miles, over 3.5 miles of Howard Greek including approximately 1 mile of spawning habitat will be destroyed for ten to fifteen years depending on recovery time.
